sources.title: Vivek Iyer and Robert M. Wald, Some Properties of Noether Charge and a Proposal for Dynamical Black Hole Entropy, Physical Review D 50 (1994), 846–864, arXiv:gr-qc/9403028v1
sources.locator: Complete 31-page PDF already retrieved and stamped in this run; inspected §3 equations (23)–(43), printed pp. 6–9 (PDF pp. 7–10); §4 equations (49)–(60), printed pp. 10–11 (PDF pp. 11–12); and §6 equations (73)–(78), (93)–(102), printed pp. 16–17 (PDF pp. 17–18). Read the first-variation curvature calculation, full charge decomposition and ambiguity, stationary horizon-charge variation, and the general surface identity.

contents.name: §3, equations (23)–(43): curvature variation, covariant potential structure and potential ambiguities
contents.support: The proof uses the derivative-free-curvature specialization of the displayed potential decomposition and states the exact Lagrangian and potential ambiguities. Matter-jet terms remain finite and covariant.

contents.name: §4, equations (49)–(60): on-shell Noether current, local charge and its general decomposition
contents.support: This is the source route for the W xi plus X nabla xi plus Y(Lie xi phi) plus exact term structure and the coefficient X=-E_R contracted with the volume form.

contents.name: §6, equations (73)–(78): stationary background identity for arbitrary linearized perturbations
contents.support: The source derives the fixed-generator surface identity from covariance, Cartan, on-shell current exactness and linearized equations. The authored item states its own residual-constraint interface explicitly.

contents.name: §6, equations (93)–(102): variation of the horizon charge at the bifurcation surface
contents.support: The calculation removes the xi and Lie-xi terms, tracks the varying binormal at fixed generator and proves the mixed normal-tangent contraction vanishes by boost/reflection invariance.

contents.name: §7 dynamical entropy proposal and higher-curvature-derivative generalization
contents.reason: This pair proves only the stationary algebraic-curvature charge variation and does not define a dynamical entropy prescription or a curvature-derivative extension.
